title: Gravity beyond starch: molecular evidence for a parallel gravity sensing mechanism
content: Unlike most environmental cues on earth, gravity is constant, omnipresent, and unidirectional. As such, it provides reliable positional information that organisms use to orient themselves, regulate their growth, and acquire essential resources (Takahashi et al. 2021). In plants, gravity directs growth and shapes architecture through gravitropism, the directional growth response that orients shoots upward and roots downward. However, this response is fine-tuned by other environmental conditions including light, nutrients, and water (Nakayama et al. 2012; Vandenbrink et al. 2019).
